summary: Relaxes the IANA allocation rules for the Protocol for Carrying Authentication for Network Access (PANA), making it easier to register new values. It is a proposed standard.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 5872 changes the approval rules for five PANA registries so the IESG can consider some allocations that do not meet the default rule. It updates RFC 5191 and leaves the other PANA registries unchanged.

questions: which pana registries allow iesg approval
subtitle: More than one approval path for registering selected PANA values

tldr.problem: Some special PANA allocations may be useful even when they do not meet the default allocation rule.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 5872 updates five PANA registries to permit IESG Approval as well as the existing allocation path for their values.
tldr.outcome: The RFC updates RFC 5191 and leaves other PANA registries unchanged.

today: RFC 5872 updates RFC 5191 with revised IANA allocation rules for five PANA registries.

sections.title: Why the Rules Changed
sections.content:
The RFC changes IANA rules for PANA, the Protocol for Carrying Authentication for Network Access. Its authors say some allocations may make sense under special circumstances even when they do not meet the default rule.

Allowing IESG Approval gives the Internet Engineering Steering Group a way to consider such requests. The RFC gives an experimental protocol extension using reserved flag bits as an example, provided enough bits remain for other purposes and the PANA community supports the allocation.
sections.plainLanguage: Some PANA values may need an exception to the usual approval route. The update lets the IESG consider those requests while keeping the existing default rules in place.

sections.title: The Five Affected Registries
sections.content:
The update affects Message Types, Message Flags, AVP Flags, Result-Code AVP Values and Termination-Cause AVP Values. Message Types and the two AVP value registries now allow IETF Review or IESG Approval instead of IETF Review only. Message Flags and AVP Flags allow Standards Action or IESG Approval instead of Standards Action only.

All other PANA IANA registries remain unchanged. The existing defined values and ranges are not rewritten by this document; it changes the allocation rules.
sections.plainLanguage: The RFC changes how five groups of PANA values can be approved. It adds IESG Approval as an option and does not change the other PANA registries.

sections.title: Experimental Values and Security
sections.content:
The RFC says it does not change PANA's security properties. It warns that experimental message values do not guarantee interoperability between a PANA Client and a PANA Authentication Agent.

Before deploying experimental values across networks that the experiment owner does not entirely control, possible harmful side effects need careful evaluation. The RFC directs readers to follow RFC 3692 guidance for experimental values.
sections.plainLanguage: This update does not change PANA's security properties. Experimental values may not work between different peers, so assess possible harm before using them on networks you do not control.
